impl.summary: Implemented the user's design in the idenso component planner (workspace /shared/codex/dev/gammaloop/idenso-planner-opaque-spectators, bookmark idenso-planner-opaque-spectators, change oorxpwzq / b31ba9cd on 58814885, author Lucien Huber, not pushed, nix-ci enable=false). Permutation-symmetric tensor heads (colour f, epsilon, symmetric/cyclic tensors without callbacks or linear/flat attributes) now enter ComponentSum as spectators: their ports stay in the incidence graph, any binding declines exactly as before, and they are emitted verbatim. Unit tests cover the four-gluon spectator-colour product (exact structure), keep-the-rest probes, vertex x vertex, equivalence with the old fallback, and epsilon/colour-metric declines; idenso (1055/1055), spenso/feynkit-generator/feynkit-graph (628/628), clippy, fmt and all 70 finite_part_ghost tests in both coupling orders (140/140) pass. BUT the design does not deliver the target on finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed: at the default coupling order it is ~1.0x upstream and 1.58-1.64x pre-#151; with wsmxownt's model-order coupling registration it removes #151's blowup (449-505 s -> 92-94 s, 0.72-0.99x pre). 17 of 34 partner-sum distributions remain because (a) the developed domains also contain gluon-propagator colour metrics g(coad,coad) that relabel f's colour slots (f then carries a contracted slot and, per the decision, keeps declining), and (b) the largest 6xN products are declined for colour trace()/chain() notation and Q(k,mink)^2 under rank_one=false, unrelated to symmetric heads. With #151's partner-sum arm disabled, the planner fix is 0.86-0.88x (default order) and 0.54-0.73x (wsmxownt order) of pre-#151, suggesting it would deliver only together with a scoped #151 restriction, which is the user's decision.
impl.design: Where/why the planner declined: ComponentSum::tensor (crates/idenso/src/shorthands/schoonschip/slot_contraction/components.rs) required `plain(head)`, which rejected every symmetric/antisymmetric/cyclic head; contract_states then returned None for any term containing colour f, contract_component refused, contract_graph returned None when no other component changed, and SymbolicTensor::contract (tensor/contract.rs) fell back to contract_ordered -> SchoonschipWithSettings::run_observed -> SlotContraction::run/find_contraction, where #151's Add-partner arm distributes the product; contract.rs retries the planner only on the rewritten result. Change (one owner, the existing participation analysis): `plain` becomes `head() -> Head {Plain, Symmetric, Opaque}` (Symmetric = only permutation symmetry; callbacks, evaluation, linear, flat, wildcards stay Opaque). tensor() admits Symmetric heads as TensorSource::Spectator: explicit permitted ports are registered as usual (degree/dummy checks, spectator-spectator and spectator-tensor shared labels stay checked); a new bind() used by all reduce_components binding arms declines when a spectator argument would change (vector substitution, metric relabelling, metric-path shortcut), and tensor() declines when an earlier selected factor's override already bound a spectator port. Spectators are emitted with their written arguments (FunctionBuilder on unchanged canonical args = identical atom). Residual spectators re-enter via tensor_with_arguments with the same Spectator source, so bind() applies across states. Alpha-memo keys stay value-safe (equal keys = consistent dummy renaming). Chains/traces (no tensor tag), untagged SYM/ANTISYM projectors and the CYCLIC projector (normalization callback) still decline; scalar spectators, factored sums, inexact coefficients inside participating sums and powers keep their existing treatment; the literal contractor and #151 are unchanged. Antisymmetric heads carrying a contracted slot (epsilon(a,..)*p(a), or f relabelled by a colour metric) keep today's path because rebuilding would reorder/sign-flip bound arguments and #151's literal fallback owns that case. Design note is in the change description.

impl.pr_title: idenso: contract around symmetric spectator tensors in the component planner
impl.pr_body:
## Summary

The component planner of `SymbolicTensor::contract` declined every symmetric, antisymmetric or cyclic tensor head, including colour structure constants that carry none of the contracted slots. A four-gluon-like vertex sum times a momentum sum sharing Lorentz slots

```
(f(a1,a2,e)*f(a3,a4,e)*(g(m1,m3)*g(m2,m4)-g(m1,m4)*g(m2,m3)) + 2 more colour terms)
  * (p1(m1)*p2(m4) + y*g(m1,m4))
```

therefore went to the literal fallback, which since #151 substitutes each source term into its own copy of the partner sum. With this change the planner contracts it and keeps every `f` as written:

```
C1*p1(m3)*p2(m2) + (y - D*y - p1.p2)*C1*g(m2,m3)
+ C2*p1(m2)*p2(m3) + (y - D*y - p1.p2)*C2*g(m2,m3)
+ C3*p1(m2)*p2(m3) - C3*p1(m3)*p2(m2)
```

(`Ci` the products of two structure constants of the source.)

Cause: `ComponentSum::tensor` required a plain head. Any symmetric head declined the whole component, and with no other progress the typed contraction fell back to `contract_ordered`.

Change: a head whose only non-plain attributes are permutation symmetries enters the planner as a spectator. Its explicit ports still join the incidence graph, so degree and dummy checks stay as they are, but no contraction may bind them. A vector substitution, a metric relabelling or a port already bound by an earlier selected factor declines the component exactly as before. Spectators are emitted with their written arguments.

What does not change: antisymmetric heads that carry a contracted slot (`epsilon(a,...)*p(a)`, or a colour metric `g(coad(a),coad(b))` relabelling an `f`) are still declined and keep #151's literal fallback. #151's two tests pass unchanged. Heads with normalization callbacks, evaluation, linear or flat attributes, chain/trace notation and projectors still decline. Scalar spectators, factored sums, powers and the literal contractor are unchanged.

`nix-ci.nix` keeps `enable = false` during review.

### Context

Found while rebasing the generation stack. In `test_renormalization::finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed`, #151's fallback distributed epsilon-free products of QCD three- and four-gluon vertex sums (34 distributions). The planner had declined them because of the spectator colour `f`. The resulting series-expansion inputs made the test about 1.5x slower, and up to 4-5x slower when the UFO coupling symbols are registered in model order.

## Tests and measurements

- New `components::tests::symmetric_spectators_stay_verbatim_beside_planned_contractions`:
  - exact planner and typed output for the example above;
  - a factored scalar, a foreign tensor, a float and a symbolic power factor pass through unchanged;
  - a vertex x vertex product stays in the planner, with every `f` as written and no `f` inside a nested sum.
- New `components::tests::symmetric_spectator_contractions_match_the_literal_rewrite`:
  - equal to the old `contract_ordered` result after expansion, for three gluon-vertex products;
  - `epsilon` with a vector-bound slot still declines, and so does `f` with a colour-metric-bound slot.
- `cargo nextest run -p idenso --lib`: 1055 passed. `-p spenso -p feynkit-generator -p feynkit-graph --lib`: 628 passed. Clippy `-D warnings` (default and `reference-cases`) and `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- All 70 `finite_part_ghost_*` tests pass with unchanged references, with both coupling registration orders.
- `finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed`, wall seconds over 3 concurrent rounds (default coupling order / model-order couplings):
  - #151 (upstream): 103-107 / 449-505
  - pre-#151: 67-69 / 95-128
  - this change: 105-110 / 92-94
- At the default order this change is therefore 1.58-1.64x pre-#151 and no faster than upstream; with model-order couplings it is 0.72-0.99x pre-#151, and #151's blowup is gone. 17 of the 34 distributions remain:
  - 3x3 four-gluon domains in which the gluon propagators' colour metrics relabel the `f`s;
  - 6xN products declined for colour `trace`/`chain` notation and squared open vectors under `rank_one = false`.
- With #151's partner-sum branch disabled, this change is 0.86-0.88x / 0.54-0.73x of pre-#151.
- d42/d43/d44 are unchanged.
- Callgrind on the traced products, Ir of the contraction:
  - isolated 3x3 product: 10.8 M -> 15.4 M, output 4463 -> 4033 bytes;
  - 3x6 product: 5.8 M -> 3.1 M, output 2131 -> 866 bytes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
open_issues: Target missed at the default coupling order: the developed test is 1.58-1.64x pre-#151 (about 1.0x upstream). With wsmxownt's model-order registration it is 0.72-0.99x pre-#151. ready=false.

17 of 34 partner-sum distributions remain with the fix. (a) The 3x3 four-gluon domains also contain gluon-propagator colour metrics g(coad,coad) that relabel f's colour slots. f then carries a contracted slot, so under the user's rule it keeps declining; the user's premise (declined only because of a spectator f) holds for only half of the distributions. (b) The 6xN products (the largest replacements, 68-75 KB) decline for colour trace()/chain() notation and Q(k,mink(dim,i))^2 under rank_one=false, unrelated to symmetric heads.

Evidence for the user's decision: an uncommitted experiment that also lets metrics relabel spectator ports leaves 12 distributions and is 1.24-1.27x pre-#151 at the default order. The planner fix with #151's partner-sum arm disabled is 0.86-0.88x / 0.54-0.73x of pre-#151 (order ratio 1.17-1.19). Disabling the arm fails #151's two tests, so this is only a proxy for 'planner fix + a scoped #151 restriction'. That restriction is the user's call; they rejected the epsilon-only draft.
Remaining order sensitivity with the fix: the model-order run takes 0.85-0.89x the default-order time (upstream 4.2-4.9x, pre-#151 1.42-1.86x).
